assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new classification of electronic phases by band topology, with protected edge and surface states. The concept is original, clear and has reshaped condensed matter physics, materials science and quantum-device thinking for nearly two decades.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group gave the decisive early experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells. This theory plus experiment trio is a natural configuration. Other contributors (e.g. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang on HgTe; Fu, Kane; Hasan and others on 3D materials) are outside the supplied credit and the allocation may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple independent material systems with spectroscopic and transport evidence; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority questions between the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposals, and over three-dimensional topological insulators, are not resolved by the supplied credit; I rely on my own recollection of these facts and have not verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping, brought fractional uncertainties to the 1e-18 level and opens routes to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a redefinition of the second. It is a clear, concrete and lasting advance in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early clocks; Ye's group pushed strontium lattice clocks to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. The two-person configuration is clean, and leaves room for a third laureate only if the committee judged a distinct contributor decisive.
assessment.maturity: Multiple groups worldwide have reproduced and improved the performance; the technology is mature and in use in metrology institutes. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Hall, Hansch and Wineland-type clock recognition already exists (2005, 2012), so the committee may judge the marginal novelty smaller; the role of ion-clock and comb contributions relative to lattice clocks is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides strong coupling of microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms and underlies dispersive readout, qubit coupling and bus architecture in superconducting quantum processors. It is conceptually elegant and has transformed quantum technology. I note my own field proximity and weigh the candidate on its merits.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues gave the theory proposal (with Girvin and Huang, outside the supplied credit), Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first strong-coupling experiments at Yale. The three supplied names can support a fair prize, but Girvin's and Devoret's roles and the interplay with the 2025 prize make allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by dozens of groups and by commercial platforms. Recognition may be considered close to the 2025 prize for superconducting circuits, which could argue for waiting, but scientifically it is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may reduce the committee's appetite for a second superconducting-circuit award so soon.
Credit beyond the three supplied names (notably Girvin) cannot be assigned here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a bandgap-engineered unipolar semiconductor laser, an invention of broad impact in mid-infrared and terahertz sources, spectroscopy, sensing and gas detection. It demonstrates a design principle from quantum engineering turned into robust devices.
assessment.attribution: The 1994 Bell Labs invention is credited to Faist, Capasso and colleagues, with Cho's molecular-beam epitaxy growth essential. A three-person prize is plausible; Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson and Kazarinov-Suris's earlier proposal are outside the supplied names and may be raised.
assessment.maturity: Commercially established and widely replicated for three decades; no maturity concern.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is seen as physics or engineering; the Kazarinov-Suris 1971 proposal and the allocation among Bell Labs coauthors are unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion quantum computation combines the Cirac-Zoller gate proposal with high-fidelity multi-qubit experiments, establishing a leading platform for quantum information processing with long coherence and gate fidelities among the best known.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt's group performed key demonstrations including the gate and teleportation. Wineland and Monroe are outside the supplied credit; Wineland already shared the 2012 prize for ion control, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Replicated across many groups and now in commercial machines; the physics is well confirmed. Timeliness is reasonable, but the 2012 prize and the 2025 prize reduce the room for another quantum-computing award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and the question of whether the Cirac-Zoller contribution is better recognised in a broader atomic quantum-information candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, with flat bands predicted by theory and correlated insulators and superconductivity observed in 2018. It is original, widely influential and has generated a large field with a tunable platform for correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. The three names form a clear theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Cao, Fatemi and others in the experimental team and earlier theory work by Lopes dos Santos et al. may be disputed.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation exists from many labs, but the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, so interpretation is not fully settled and recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Priority claims on the theory side.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with controllable parameters, as in the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and have created the field of analogue quantum simulation of many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and colleagues proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch performed the Mott insulator experiment and developed quantum-gas microscopes. The supplied four names exceed three, so I choose the three I judge decisive; Cirac's role is real but I judge it secondary here.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and extended; recognition is mature, though the Bose-Einstein condensation prizes of 2001 and 1997/2012 laser cooling prizes overlap in subject.
uncertainties: Which of the four supplied names should be omitted is a judgement and may be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction codes, together with the threshold theorem and topological codes, show that large-scale quantum computation is possible in principle. This matters to me directly because full-scale error correction is the technical requirement for useful processors.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane produced the first quantum error-correcting codes; Kitaev introduced topological protection and fault-tolerant ideas. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and Aharonov-Ben-Or also contributed and are outside the supplied names, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Theory is long established, and experiments recently show below-threshold logical qubits on superconducting and atomic platforms. Experimental maturity is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Experimental demonstration of scalable fault tolerance is incomplete.
Substantial credit disputes beyond the supplied names.
